newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian police probe station blast that killed two.
newsitem.headline: Russian police probe station blast that killed two.

text.p: Russian police were trying on Thursday to determine who or what caused an explosion which killed two people at a railway station in the southern town of Armavir.
Chechen separatist leaders who fought a nearly 21-month conflict with Moscow denied any involvement in Wednesday's blast, which Itar-Tass news agency said was so powerful it blew a woman to pieces.

It said another woman died in hospital and about eight people were hurt, including a 10-year-old boy who had serious head injuries. Local police officials revised downwards initial reports that up to 20 people had been hurt.
Police and troops sealed off the station and hunted into the night for possible bombers under the glare of floodlights.
Tass quoted local police as saying an explosive device may have gone off in a passenger's bag at the ticket office or in the waiting room and that this would explain why one body was ripped apart.
They said the woman appeared to have been a local tramp, although final identification was not yet possible.

Armavir is about 320 km (200 miles) west of the separatist region of Chechnya and the railway line goes to the Chechen capital Grozny, prompting speculation that the explosion was caused by a Chechen bomb.
Asked if he ruled out a Chechen connection, a duty police officer in the main regional city of Krasnodar told Reuters: "How could anyone possibly rule that out?"
Radical Chechen separatists have threatened to launch attacks on southern Russian cities to avenge the death of independence leader Dzhokhar Dudayev on April 21 last year.

But Chechen vice-president Vakha Arsanov, who is standing in for President Aslan Maskhadov while he is away on a Moslem pilgrimage, said "Chechen resistance forces" were not involved and blamed the incident on Russian special forces.
Chechen Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev echoed his words.

"Until the investigative organs establish the cause of the explosion at the railway station in Armavir, it is unfair to put us in the position of having to explain ourselves over any crime outside Chechnya," he told RIA news agency.

Separatist guerrillas staged two bloody hostage-taking raids outside Chechnya during the conflict with Russia. The organiser of one of them, Salman Raduyev, has vowed to stage new attacks, including on Russia's rail network.

A ceasefire was agreed last August in Chechnya, after the deaths of tens of thousands of people, but talks are bogged down over the region's demands for complete independence, which Moscow has ruled out.
Several blasts disrupted the Moscow transport system during the Chechnya conflict. Police have failed to solve those cases.
Two bombs exploded and another was found before it went off in three incidents on a railway line near Volgograd in southern Russia last summer.
In Moscow, more than 30 people were hurt in two bomb explosions on trolleybuses last July. Four people died in a bomb blast on the city underground rail network the previous month.
